q:
The nausea started to ease like 2 weeks ago or so, but yesterday I woke up feeling absolutely awful. Today has been better but I still feel like crap.   
I thought I was finally almost done with it, but I’m worried I’m falling back into it again.
cx: 11 weeks, sickness returning after a lull.

q: I als am SO tired of this horrible taste in my mouth. It doesn’t matter what I eat, whether it’s sour, sweet, bland, salty, WATER, ANYTHING. Nothing helps.
cx: 11 weeks.

q: I just found out that my daily moisturiser got Retinyl Palmitate in the ingredients list! :(
cx: 17 weeks, after reading an ingredient list.

q: When I said this he just screwed his face up and said he can’t recommend it.
cx: UK, 37 weeks, asking a consultant for a midwife-unit birth after a first caesarean.

q: Then came the other issue of booking the scan and review appointment, there aren’t any available in the next two weeks. So now I’m just stuck in limbo
cx: Her birth plan sign-off depends on a scan she can't book.

q: I’m a planner and like to have these things organised and now I’m stressing because I literally have like a day to decide or try and convince him differently 😬 help haha
cx: UK, 16 weeks, planning how to tell both grandfathers.

q: I just wanted to let you know that it's not all about your pain tolerance or amount of mental/physical preparation. Some people just get lucky.
cx: A mother sharing why some people describe birth as easy.

q: Sadly (for me), my mom also described her 4 unmedicated births as "mostly pressure, nothing too bad" and I definitely, definitely do not agree.
cx: Her mother's account of birth versus her own.

q: We currently live in a camper cause every form of housing where we are is $1600+/mo to rent or $280,000 to buy a nearly condemned house.
cx: 20-year-old first-time mother, married, due in August.

q: It was a small business with my boss/the owner and me the only people in office, a few remote employees, and HR (only here since late March) was the boss’s mom. I was not being given any, much less proper accommodations for my pregnancy
cx: Why she quit a night-shift job in her second trimester.

q: my boss wouldn’t allow me to eat or go to the bathroom while I worked the 5 hour shifts 7 days a week.
cx: Trying to follow a diet plan her midwife gave her.

q: I used to think it was easy to be good while pregnant, just no drugs or alcohol right? Simple enough! …Then I step into that hospital room and get an ancient scroll’s worth of the “what not to do’s”.
cx: First-time mother blaming herself after a worrying scan.

q: The next nearest ones that take our insurance and have good feedback by family/friends living in the areas are 3-6 hours away and I can’t afford the extra fuel cost, much less food or possible overnights. Especially with the increased frequency in visits
cx: Rural; her midwife is the only nearby option.

q: It’s so hard being in this place of “I don’t want to know everything that COULD go wrong, but also, absolutely tell me every single thing that could go wrong”
cx: On wanting her midwife to be warmer.

q: Our financial situation is rocky at best, and we’re barely making our bills on time, so buying anything for baby is out of the question. I can’t really throw a baby shower, again because of the finances
cx: A week later, still nothing bought for the baby.

q: My husband had to go back to work yesterday so no more help with nighttime care.
cx: Two weeks after the birth, first wave of overwhelm at 5am.

q: I also moved the baby and me into the living room, but my partner is still in the bedroom so I feel a sadness bc we're separated physically.
cx: After her partner's return to work.

q: I absolutely DREAD my prenatal appointments because the very first thing they do is check your weight. Mine always goes up by at least 10 lbs, and it just puts a damper on my entire appointment.
cx: 28 weeks with second pregnancy.

q: I’m thinking about telling my midwife that I’d rather weigh myself and home and report back, or get weighed there but ask that they keep it off the chart so I can’t see it.
cx: Her idea to make check-ups bearable.

q: I also work part time (20-30 hrs) for family business which is very, very low effort but it’s necessary for me to stay employed as our insurance is through me.
cx: First-time mother due in December, planning a fall practicum; crossposted.

q: I’ll be in my 3rd trimester for the entirety of the semester but I’ve never been pregnant before so I have no idea what to expect.
cx: Planning months ahead with no reference point.

q: If I end up dropping mid-semester, I would not get refunded for the classes. Similarly, in my experience 12/6 always falls before final projects/exams are due… so this worries me
cx: Weighing whether to register for fall.

q: Im not telling my team until 2nd trimester. I’m lucky to be at home 3 days a week but I work from the couch and sleep on my breaks. And the days I go into the office are unbearable.
cx: First-time mother at 8 weeks, full-time desk job.

q: We constantly have lunch catered and last week it was some sort of salmon or seafood situation and I had to work in the lobby the rest of the day for how horrible it made the office smell.
cx: Hiding first-trimester sickness at the office.

q: BIL has not been disrespectful or a major privacy concern but I'm so upset that I can't just walk around my house belly out or braless without the possibility of running into him.
cx: 24 weeks; husband's brother has lived with them for six months.

q: I'm worried about getting my need for privacy and the desired intimacy of this time met and if I'm mad now, I can't imagine how I might feel while dealing with post partum and the first months of my baby's life.
cx: Four months before the due date.

q: Husband had a vague and brief talk with him instead that hinted at this 🫠
cx: She wanted a clear ask that he move out before the birth.

q: This is my second baby and felt extremely overwhelmed with my first born because I allowed visitors ALL the time (I didn’t want anyone over I felt pressure from my family). I felt very overwhelmed, constantly cleaning the house, providing food for people, entertaining, skipping pumps (I didn’t know any better), etc. it was horrible.
cx: Six weeks after her second birth, with a no-visitors rule this time.

q: With that said now that I’ve had my second we only have had two best friends over (they provided food, helped me clean, took the baby so I can sleep).
cx: Her second-baby visitor rule.

q: Now I am feel a lot of pressure from my extended family (who I see once a year) to “finally” meet my newborn.
cx: Texts from relatives at six weeks postpartum.

q: My aunt and uncle showed up to my house and wouldn’t leave until we answers the door. They needed to meet the baby.
cx: Despite a six-week no-visitors rule.

q: (P.s I come from a different culture where we are expected to serve our guests, entertain, etc.)
cx: Why visits mean work for her.

q: My milk supply dropped so much the first time around because I didn’t really understand the whole process and felt all this pressure from relatives that we see hardly ever.
cx: Looking back on her first baby's early weeks.

q: I am surrounded by women, like my mom and aunts that say they have never had issues like this and I honestly think that I might be over reacting.
cx: 39 weeks, barely able to move.

q: And the worst part is, that I am so dependent on the people around me... I almost can't do anything on my own. Can't cook, can't do the laundry, clean, go to the store...
cx: Formerly very active, now at 39 weeks.

q: And the uncertainty of the fact that labor could start any moment but also be weeks away is killing me.
cx: 39 weeks.

q: I was just informed that my doctor will be on leave starting June 21st. He said not to worry since this is my second time giving birth and usually babies come earlier than 40 weeks.
cx: 33 weeks; due June 22nd.

q: Plus, he will do membrane sweep at 39 weeks and 90% it will induce labor.
cx: Doctor's plan before his leave.

q: I am trying to keep my worries as less as possible and hearing from a fellow person who went through same things really makes a difference.
cx: Under 7 weeks, worried when symptoms faded.

q: he’s said ‘you’re such an emotional wreck’, ‘why are you so serious all the time’ and this one takes the crown, ‘you’re pulling the pregnant card’.
cx: Nine months pregnant with a toddler; husband always on work calls.

q: He never stops working from his phone, he never stops taking work related calls, he never stops accommodating other people and their needs.
cx: Self-employed husband during her pregnancy.

q: I keep thinking about how people manage things like childcare, getting a break, or even going on dates, and it’s making me feel really lost and kind of alone in all of this.
cx: Just found out at about 3 weeks; family not close, in-laws far away.

q: raised in a very “it takes a village” environment, and I helped raise my siblings and take care of a lot growing up. Now I’m not close with my family, it’s just me and my husband, and his family lives far away.
cx: Why support feels missing so early.

q: He says the bump freaks him out.
cx: 25 weeks, first child; partner no longer interested in sex.

q: He said he wouldn’t go if I didn’t want him to, but clearly wanted to, and honestly, we could always use extra money with a baby on the way, so I said it was fine.
cx: Partner offered weeks of out-of-town work.
